analysis.title: FirstEnergy Corp. (FE): Raising estimates on transmission upside, further opportunity in WV; Buy
key_insights: GS keeps FE at Buy and raises the 12-month price target to $55 from $53, based on 17.5x P/E (unchanged) on Q5-Q8 estimates, a 1x premium over GS's baseline. Price was $46.83 at the 29 Oct 2026 close, implying 17.4% upside.

After 3Q26 results, FE expects transmission investment to rise by at least 25% versus its current $19bn 2026-30 plan as it rolls the plan forward to 2027-31. Management said most of the increase comes from broader reliability and resiliency needs rather than data centers.
FE still assumes about $250mn of transmission investment per 1 GW of contracted load. Contracted data center demand rose to 7.9 GW, with about 4 GW more in active negotiations.
GS raises 2027-30 transmission capex estimates by about $3.5bn, adding EPS upside of 1% in 2028, 2% in 2029 and 2% in 2030. GS now sees an 8.6% EPS CAGR through 2030, up from 8.0%.

West Virginia is the main upside source. A CPCN decision (state siting approval) for the Maidsville generation project is expected in 4Q26, and FE has reserved turbines for delivery in 2030. FE plans to update its financial plan after the order.

Beyond Maidsville, FE is in talks on another 3 GW of potential load and has issued an RFP for 3 GW of additional CCGT equipment, with longer-term generation expected in 2031-32 and beyond. It is also looking at bridge power options as soon as 2028 and weighing both rate-based and GenCo structures.

WV rate case resolved: the $76mn Inflation and Investment Adjustment was approved as filed. The first increase is effective August 1, 2026 and the second June 1, 2027, with a stay-out through April 2028.
Ohio 3-Year Rate Plan: the staff report is due November 30, 2026 and hearings begin in March 2027. GS expects the staff report to give the next read on the likely outcome.

New Jersey: the $253mn base rate case is underway, reflecting about $1bn of rate base growth since the February 2024 increase. FE proposes delaying the customer bill impact until 2028, and management expects more clarity on the state's affordability review late this year or early next.
Maryland: FE filed for a $53mn revenue increase in September, with hearings in January 2027 and an outcome expected in April 2027.

GS says FE trades at a 6% P/E discount to its coverage (ex CA) and that the valuation does not fully reflect the transmission and WV generation upside. GS sees further upside when FE gives its updated capital plan in February.

market_movers.rationale: GS raised the target from $53 to $55 on higher transmission capex and EPS estimates (8.6% EPS CAGR through 2030). Maidsville CPCN decision in 4Q26 and the February capital plan update are the next catalysts.

earnings_insights: FE 3Q26 results were reported before this note (30 Oct 2026). The note gives GS 3Q26 actual EPS of $0.98 (9/26 quarter) and does not state a consensus figure.
GS EPS estimates (GS estimates, not reported): 2026E $2.75 (old $2.74), 2027E $2.97 (old $2.96), 2028E $3.23 (old $3.20). 2025 EPS was $2.55 (reported).
Management said contracted data center demand is 7.9 GW, with about 4 GW more in active negotiations.
risk_factors: An unfavorable outcome in the Ohio rate case.
Pension expense and/or interest expense coming in higher than expected.
